newsitem.title: UK: Yorkshire B/S sees 96 profit fall after margin cut.
newsitem.headline: Yorkshire B/S sees 96 profit fall after margin cut.

text.p: Yorkshire Building Society on Tuesday posted a sharply lower pre-tax profit of 43.2 million stg in 1996 compared to 84.9 million stg in 1995 after following its policy of slashing its interest margins.
The Yorkshire cut its net interest margin 1.28 percent in 1996 and said pre-tax profit would have risen to 88.2 million stg if it had maintained its 1995 interest margin of 1.95 percent.
Assets grew by 11.4 percent to 7.14 billion stg from 6.41 billion at the end of 1995, a growth level that the society said was almost twice the industry average.

The Yorkshire, which plans to hold on to its mutual status rather than convert to bank status and float on the stock exchange, said in November 1995 that it would return the benefits of mutuality to its members.
The society's gross mortgage lending stood at 1.33 billion stg while net lending grew by 47 percent to 624 million stg.

"The Yorkshire is confident that its results in 1996 demonstrate a clear intention to deliver long-term value as a mutual organisation," Yorkshire's chief executive David Anderson. "This is only the start. We are determined to maintain our agenda and look forward to delivering real benefits to members in future."
